title: Quantized opset mismatch: recovery actions, compatibility hardening, and monitoring roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: After a model rollout containing a newer fused operator, some quantized (int8/int4) serving variants entered crash loops or returned silent accuracy regressions. This ticket tracks the immediate recovery steps taken, a set of short/medium/long-term hardening actions, and monitoring/alerting we need to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-09 02:18 UTC: On-call alert — elevated 5xx rate for several hosted customers using quantized variants; latency spikes observed as requests retried to float fallback.

2026-03-09 02:35 UTC: Initial triage — multiple models built from the new model artifact contained an operator opcode not present in our quant kernel whitelist; int8 path fell back inconsistently and triggered an allocator panic in the quant runtime on GPU nodes.

2026-03-09 03:10 UTC: Emergency hotpatch — orchestration rollback to previous model digest for affected customers; auto-fallback to float path enabled more broadly to reduce 5xxs (temporary cost increase).

2026-03-09 09:00 UTC: Post-incident table readout — identified two root contributors: (1) opset drift in model artifacts (new fused-attn op) and (2) lack of early-stage opset compatibility checks in our quant deployment pipeline. Also discovered that KV cache eviction timing interacted with allocator zeroing and surfaced as a crash in low-memory conditions.
2026-03-10 11:45 UTC: Created this action-tracking ticket to coordinate cross-team mitigation and longer-term prevention work.

2026-03-11 16:20 UTC: Hotpatch verified in prod cluster; crash loops stopped and error rates returned to baseline. Cost telemetry shows a ~12% short-lived cost increase due to float fallback during recovery window.
root_cause: Model artifact included a fused attention op variant (fused_attn_v2) that maps to an operator opcode unknown to our quant kernel selector, causing the quant path to attempt a fallback which triggered a code path with an allocator bug on specific GPU runtimes.

Deployment pipeline lacked an opset / operator fingerprint check for quant compatibility in the pre-deploy CI canary, so the incompatible model landed in production for quant variants before regression surfaced.

Insufficient telemetry for unsupported-ops at inference time — we only recorded generic fallback events, not per-op fingerprints or sequence-length conditioned failures, making root-cause correlation slower.

KV-cache eviction race with low-memory allocator: when fallback mixed quantized and float kernels in the same JVM, a corner-case zeroing path caused a null-pointer in allocator on some kernels leading to crash loops.
Automated nightly evals were checking functional outputs but not measuring per-op kernel coverage or small drift vs float baseline for the quant variant.
impact_summary: Affected hosted customers: ~11 customers experienced increased 5xxs and elevated latency during the event window.
Error budget burn: Several tenants exceeded error SLOs for a 45-minute window.
Operational cost: temporary fallback to float models increased token serving cost by ~12% for the recovery period.
Reputation: 2 customers opened support tickets escalated to SEs; NPS impact potentially medium-term.
short_term_mitigations: Rollback affected model digests from 2026-03-09 to previously verified digest — owner: Linnea Johnson — status: done (2026-03-09 03:10 UTC).
Enable conservative auto-fallback to float for customers with strict SLOs while we validate quant kernel compatibility — owner: Ops Runbook — status: done.
Add a temporary production alert metric 'quant_op_unsupported_count' with a 1-min burn rate; alert to on-call after threshold 5/min — owner: Marco Ruiz — status: done (2026-03-09 05:40 UTC).
medium_term_actions: Implement opset/operator fingerprinting at model ingestion: fail quant variant deployment if new opcodes are present unless annotated safe — owner: Marco Ruiz — due: 2026-03-20.
Expand CI canary to include quant-path unit+integration tests against the actual kernels used in prod (hardware-aware CI shard) — owner: Rahul Menon — due: 2026-04-01.
Create a dedicated allocator safety test that reproduces KV-cache eviction under low-memory stress to catch the null-pointer pattern observed — owner: Linnea Johnson — due: 2026-03-28.
Add per-op telemetry (op fingerprint + sequence length + kernel id) to tracing and sampling pipeline for easier correlation — owner: Aisha Patel — due: 2026-03-25.
Author a post-deploy checklist for model on-boarding which includes: opset report, quant kernel compatibility matrix, nightly eval pass results — owner: Product (Model Onboarding) — due: 2026-03-30.
long_term_roadmap: Automated canary rollouts for quant variants that run golden prompt suite and accuracy drift checks vs float baseline before full traffic cutover — owner: Platform Reliability — due: 2026-05-15.

Quant kernel compatibility matrix service: centralized catalog of supported ops per runtime/quant-profile, surfaced in Console and used by deployment pipeline — owner: Engineering Infra — due: 2026-06-01.
Continuous quant regression harness: nightly headless evaluation across a representative corpus with drift alerting and per-model baselines — owner: Applied ML / Evals — due: 2026-04-20.
Introduce a lightweight offline op-translation shim for certain fused ops to enable safe deploys while kernel implementations are developed — owner: Research/Runtime — due: 2026-07-01.
Runbook and incident playbook update: add quant-specific triage steps, customer communication templates, and rollback procedures — owner: SRE/Oncall — due: 2026-03-18.

postmortem_notes: We need stricter separation of float/quant deployment pipelines until the kernel compatibility catalog is live; mixing fallback strategies increased blast radius.
Improve SLAs around pre-deploy canaries: teams that own model artifacts must run quant-compat checks as part of release gating.
Telemetry gaps slowed root cause analysis — investing in per-op fingerprinting and better sampling will pay off for future heterogenous model rollouts.
Customer communication: proactive outreach template drafted — include cost impact summary and steps taken to mitigate.

Lessons learned: quant regressions are not only about accuracy drift; unsupported ops and allocator interactions create different failure modes (crash loops & latency spikes) and need distinct detection signals.
